title: Global uniqueness for isotropic elasticity
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) that the displacement-to-traction map of an isotropic elastic body determines both Lamé moduli: on a bounded connected domain in R^3 with smooth boundary, smooth moduli with μ > 0 and 3λ + 2μ > 0 are determined by the boundary map, without analyticity, smallness or agreement near the boundary. The first lesson defines the map through the energy, Korn's identity and the Dirichlet problem, and states the theorem. The second extends both pairs of moduli to R^3 so that they agree outside the domain, from the determination of their boundary jets, and transfers solutions from one medium to the other. The third adjoins the divergence as a fourth unknown, obtains a system with principal part the Laplacian, and proves a Carleman estimate and a solvability result with an exponential phase. The fourth treats planar transport equations: the Cauchy transform, frames over disks, and solutions with compact support. The fifth constructs exact complex geometrical optics solutions whose leading displacement and divergence are any prescribed solution of a transport equation on a three-dimensional space. The sixth compares the transport equations of the two media by a field that depends holomorphically on the direction, which ranges over a conic in the complex projective plane. The seventh shows that this field is the identity and recovers both moduli. Four results from the literature are used as named hypotheses: boundary determination, interior elliptic regularity for systems, a Carleman estimate for the Laplacian and the existence of holomorphic frames over a disk.
prerequisites: core course Functional Analysis (Erdman): Hilbert spaces and the Riesz-Frechet representation theorem (Section 4.4, Theorem 4.5.2)
core course Complex Analysis (Lebl): the identity theorem (Theorem 2.4.7), the Cauchy-Pompeiu formula (Theorem 4.6.3), Liouville's theorem (Theorem 3.3.10)
core course Vector Calculus (CLP-4): the divergence theorem (Theorem 4.2.2)
Lebesgue integration, L^2 spaces, distributions, the Fourier transform on R^n and Sobolev spaces H^1, H^1_0 and H^k

programme course Elliptic operators and boundary problems: Fourier transforms and Sobolev norms (lesson Fourier transforms, finite spectra and convex separation, Sections 2 and 7), compactness and smoothness of Sobolev functions (lesson Symbols, finite defects, and the index on a closed manifold, Section 1)
programme course DG-FND: weak subsequences in Hilbert space (lesson Complex manifolds and Kähler metrics, Lemma K.2)

checks.reading: The manuscript 'Global uniqueness for the smooth isotropic elasticity inverse problem' (OpenAI, 24 Sep 2026; main.tex 63 lines, introduction 217, boundary reduction 78, analytic estimates 297, physical amplitudes 412, transport matching 587, coefficient recovery 299, references.bib 229) was read in full on 15 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written: the energy bound and Korn's identity; the Dirichlet problem and the weak boundary map; the gluing of functions with equal jets, the common exterior extension and the transfer of solutions; the identities of the augmented system and the normalized operator; the semiclassical norms, the supported Carleman estimate from the convexified estimate, solvability by duality and the scaled interior estimate; the Cauchy transform, regularity for d/dz-bar, local frames, frames with parameters and inhomogeneous solutions; supported planar transport (uniqueness, estimates, left inverses and smooth dependence); the leading operators, the compatibility identities and the recursion of order N >= 4 with the correction; the transport normal form, weak limits of transferred solutions, the comparison on almost every plane and on every plane, smoothness and holomorphy in the direction; the bundle on the null conic, rigidity of the comparison, the finite-type lemma and the recovery of the moduli. No error found in the manuscript. Four cited results are kept as named hypotheses with exact statements: (BD) from Tan-Liu 2023 (Theorem 1.2), (ER) from Dyatlov's notes (Theorem 15.1, Remark 15.2, Proposition 15.6), (CE) from Salo-Tzou 2009 (Lemma 2.1 with s = -1), (HF) from Forstneric 2009 (Theorem 1.1). Differences of presentation: the course proves that continuous functions with continuous distributional derivatives are C^1, the regularity bootstrap for d/dz-bar by the Fourier transform, the quantitative smooth dependence of planar frames on parameters, and the propagation of the finite-type system along polygonal paths by Gronwall's inequality. Free sources read on 15 Oct 2026: Tan-Liu arXiv:2211.06650 (Theorem 1.2 and the introduction); Salo-Tzou arXiv:0709.2282 (Lemma 2.1); Dyatlov, 18.155 notes (Section 15.1); Forstneric arXiv:0906.2421 (Theorem 1.1); Imanuvilov-Yamamoto 2004, authors' preprint (Section 1); the arXiv abstract of Cekic arXiv:2309.09348; Erdman, Lebl and CLP-4 for the numbering of the cited core-course results. open_obligations: Hypothesis (BD) of the lesson 'Boundary jets and the transfer of solutions': if the displacement-to-traction maps of two smooth pairs with mu > 0 and lambda + mu >= 0 agree, all derivatives of the moduli agree on the boundary [Tan-Liu 2023, Theorem 1.2]. Not proved in the programme.

Hypothesis (ER) of the lesson 'Boundary jets and the transfer of solutions': interior elliptic regularity for second-order systems with smooth coefficients and invertible principal symbol, with constants uniform for a smooth family with parameters in a compact set [Dyatlov, 18.155 notes, Theorem 15.1, Remark 15.2, Proposition 15.6]. Not proved in the programme in this generality.

Hypothesis (CE) of the lesson 'An augmented system and a Carleman estimate': the semiclassical Carleman estimate from H^-1_h to H^1_h for the Laplacian with a convexified linear weight [Salo-Tzou 2009, Lemma 2.1, s = -1]. Not proved in the programme.

Hypothesis (HF) of the lesson 'Planar transport equations': for smooth A on a disk, d/dz-bar V = A V has an invertible solution on the whole disk (holomorphic triviality of vector bundles over a disk) [Forstneric 2009, Theorem 1.1]. Not proved in the programme.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
